messages:
marie: heads up — since ~09:10 UTC we saw a sharp tail-latency spike for gpu-attach in us-west3. provisioning requests are queuing and a few attaches hit 30s+ and then fail. logs point at local NVMe IO stall during ephemeral-cleaner runs.

devon: saw that too, 09:12 window. iostat shows write_iops jump and avg await balloon. attaching quick snippets below.

marie: iostat output:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await
nvme0n1         12.00  1450.00  1024.00  81920.00  48.2
nvme1n1          1.00   980.00   128.00  65536.00  52.9
```

akshay: those wkB/s numbers align with janitor deep-scrub running across many nodes. janitor schedule overlapped with a batch GPU job rollout. scrub bursts + continuous batching = IO amplification.

ben: also seeing SMART warnings on some hosts (increased media_err_cnt). not full corruption but drive retries spike which amplifies latency.

marie: janitor-bot reported concurrent runs: `janitor-bot: starting deep-scrub job group/ephemeral/2026-03-20T09:08Z on nodeset us-west3-prod-2`

lina: can we throttle janitor concurrency and lower scrubbing batch size immediately? that should reduce write burst. ops-scheduler, can you spike throttle?

ops-scheduler: scheduled a quick mitigation — reduced janitor concurrency from 12 -> 3 on us-west3 and enabled 5s sleep between file batches. will monitor.

devon: re: quick telemetry — the health scoring is too sensitive to short retry spikes. it's flipping nodes to READONLY prematurely and that causes host-level fsync backpressure. suggest smoothing retry metric with a 2m EWMA and require sustained >3% retry rate before READONLY.

akshay: agreed. short-term: a) throttle janitor, b) add NVMe retry hysteresis in health-agent, c) route gpu-attach to other AZs while node recovers.

ben: for longer term we should: - stagger scrubs across partitions, - add per-node scrubbing windows tied to low-provisioning forecasts, - mark drives with rising media_err_cnt for lower scrub priority instead of immediate quarantine.

marie: rolled a temporary routing rule to prefer eu-west1 and us-east1 for attaches if us-west3 avg attach latency > 5s. traffic shift ~22% away. attach failures dropped.

janitor-bot: note: postponed scheduled deep-scrub tasks on 42 nodes (us-west3) until 2026-03-20T13:00Z.

devon: can someone paste the nvme-cli errors we saw? i saw a pattern of `nvme_err: media_read_retry` followed by `blk_rq issue` spam. that retry loop + fsync waits are the killer.

marie: sample dmesg lines:
```
[Mar 20 09:11:23] nvme0n1: media read retry 7
[Mar 20 09:11:24] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[Mar 20 09:11:24] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): delayed block allocation failed for inode 34567
```

lina: cost question — if we keep redirecting attaches to other regions during scrub windows we'll increase cross-region egress and reserved GPU use. ops, what's the estimated delta?

ops-scheduler: rough calc: 22% traffic shift for ~2h = ~0.6 GPU-hours extra on other regions and ~40GB egress. cost impact ~ $6-$12 for this incident window. cheaper than SLA/attach failures though.

akshay: risk note: we also saw a small uptick in container restarts because kubelet saw node pressure when scrub IO blocked pagecache writeback. lowering scrub write rate solves that.

marie: current status — attach latency back under 2s after throttles and routing. continuing 15m watch. plan: patch health-agent to smooth NVMe retry metric (PR ready), implement staggered scrub rollout, and add a canary for health threshold change in us-west3 only.

devon: PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/janitor/pull/612 (throttle + sleeper)

ben: i'll open a followup to add a drive-state tiering policy so we deprioritize heavy ops on drives with rising retries.

marie: thanks team. if things re-spike ping @oncall. leaving thread open for post-mortem notes. :white_check_mark:
